name: co.agentready/connectors
title: Agent Ready
description: Rank, tools and history of every connector in ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Muse and other AI app stores

tools.name: search_connectors
tools.description: Use this when the user wants a list of connectors, plugins, apps or MCP servers in the AI app stores (ChatGPT plugins, Claude connectors and plugins, Cursor, Gemini, Grok, Google Search, Muse): the top-ranked ones in a store, the highest-ranked consumer (B2C) connector, ones with a feature (OAuth, UI, server instructions, app events, skills over MCP, a hosting provider) or ones in a category. Returns observed directory listings, not platform compatibility; absence does not mean unsupported. Returns slugs for get_connector. To look up several brands or connectors by name, pass them all in names in one call. Do not use it to count; use analyze.

q.description: Words in the connector name, company, description or keywords

rank_max.description: Overall rank in `store` (chatgpt or claude) this high or better, e.g. 100. Not the rank within a category: with category, use a larger value (e.g. 1000) for the top of that category

audience.description: Who it is for; consumer is closest to B2C

category.description: Agent Ready category slug, e.g. travel, finance, dev-code

kind.description: connector (tools or an MCP server) or skills (skill pack only)

has_events.description: Has ChatGPT plugin events (not MCP notifications); list them with search_components type=event

mcp_notification.description: Declares this standard MCP notification (not ChatGPT plugin events)

has_ui.description: Shows an interactive widget in the chat

host_provider.description: Hosting provider, from the server host name

tools_known.description: Its tool list is known (false: hidden behind sign-in)

auth_provider.description: Sign-in provider of its OAuth server

dynamic_registration.description: OAuth server supports dynamic client registration

cimd.description: OAuth server accepts client ID metadata documents

anonymous_tools.description: Some tools work before signing in

released_after.description: Released on or after this date (YYYY-MM-DD)

sort.description: rank and trend need `store` (rank: chatgpt or claude; trend: claude only). Without a store, rank uses the best rank in any store. newest sorts by release date; keywords sorts by how many ChatGPT plugin keywords a listing has (each row gives keyword_count; get_connector lists them)

limit.description: How many connectors to return, 1 to 100

names.description: Look up several connectors at once: 1 to 25 brand names, connector names or web domains, in place of q. Gives up to 3 best matches per name, each with matched_name, and lists names with no match in not_found. Use this, not one call per name

intent.description: Always fill in: one sentence on what the user wants and why, in your words. No personal details.

tools.name: get_connector
tools.description: Use this when you need one connector's data without showing it, or data the card lacks (to show a connector to the user, use render_connector_detail): rank in each store, tools and what they can do, skills, sign-in, hosting, server instructions and example prompts. Also returns the app events it lists (separate from MCP notifications), where its instructions come from, and what we could not see. Empty catalogs may be hidden behind sign-in. Store presence is not platform compatibility; current skills are not evidence of recent additions. Use include_tools=false and include_instructions=false for a concise overview. Set full_tools=true for every stored tool and full descriptions. Use get_connector_changelog for historical changes. Search only when the slug is unknown. Returns the MCP server URL when known.

include_tools.description: Include tools. Set false for a concise overview; legacy default is true

include_instructions.description: Include full server instructions; set false for an overview

full_tools.description: Return every stored tool with full descriptions and stored parameter details instead of the legacy 40-tool preview

intent.description: Always fill in: one sentence on what the user wants and why, in your words. No personal details.

tools.name: get_connector_changelog
tools.description: Use this when a user asks what changed in a named app, whether tools were added or removed, how an MCP server evolved, or whether a ChatGPT app was updated. Accepts one slug or an array for comparison in one call, e.g. slug=["seatgeek","linear"], store=chatgpt. Returns chronological changes with before/after evidence, coverage dates, limitations and per-connector pagination. Prefer this over list_changes for named connectors. Never substitute rank history for functional changes. Known slugs need no search first.

slug.description: Known slug or up to 10 slugs to compare, e.g. ["seatgeek", "linear"]. Search only if the slug is unknown

kinds.description: Change types in one request; omit for all

limit.description: Maximum events per connector per page

cursor.description: next_cursor from the previous page, with the same filters

intent.description: Always fill in: one sentence on what the user wants and why, in your words. No personal details.

tools.name: get_rank_history
tools.description: Use this when the user asks how one connector's rank changed over time in the ChatGPT plugin directory or the Claude directory. Gives the rank and the store size for each day. Only ChatGPT and Claude publish a rank. Use for directory position or popularity ranking, NOT functionality or tool changes; use get_connector_changelog for those.

store.description: chatgpt or claude: the only stores that publish a rank

from.description: First day (YYYY-MM-DD). Leave out for the whole history

to.description: Last day (YYYY-MM-DD). Leave out for the latest day

intent.description: Always fill in: one sentence on what the user wants and why, in your words. No personal details.

tools.name: search_tools
tools.description: Use this when the user asks which connectors have a certain kind of tool or input, for example a send-feedback tool, a booking tool, or inputs that capture user intent or context. Searches tool names, titles, descriptions, input names and input descriptions across every connector, and returns each tool with its inputs. Combine with connector filters (store, category, audience, rank_max). Without q, lists the tools of the matching connectors.

q.description: Words to find in tool names, titles, descriptions, input names and input descriptions, for example "feedback" or "user intent". Leave out to list the tools of the matching connectors

match.description: Where q must match: any (default), name (tool name or title), description (tool description), inputs (an input's name or description)

access.description: Only tools with this access (declared by the server, else estimated from the name)

source.description: store: tools the store lists. server: tools only the MCP server lists, not the store

connector.description: Words in the connector's name, company or description, to search one connector or a few

rank_max.description: Overall rank in `store` (chatgpt or claude) this high or better, e.g. 100. Not the rank within a category: with category, use a larger value (e.g. 1000) for the top of that category

tools.name: search_components
tools.description: Use this when the user asks about skills, commands, hooks, agents, rules, prompts, UI templates (interactive widgets), app events (type=event: the events each connector declares, with their descriptions), desktop extensions or other parts of plugins and connectors besides tools: which connectors have them, or ones about a topic. Filter by type and connector filters.

type.description: Only this kind of component: skill, command, agent, subagent, hook, rule, prompt, app, ui_template (an interactive UI), event (a ChatGPT plugin event), desktop_extension, and others

q.description: Words to find in the component's name, label or description

connector.description: Words in the connector's name, company or description, to search one connector or a few

rank_max.description: Overall rank in `store` (chatgpt or claude) this high or better, e.g. 100. Not the rank within a category: with category, use a larger value (e.g. 1000) for the top of that category

tools.name: analyze
tools.description: Use this when the user asks for any count or statistic about connectors, tools, tool inputs or components (skills, commands, UI templates...): how many, broken down by up to 2 fields, with min, max, mean, median and 90th percentile of numbers such as tools per connector, description length or inputs per tool. Examples: max and mean tools per connector in Claude (entity=connectors, store=claude, measure=["tools"]); input types by store (entity=inputs, group_by=["store","type"]); skills per category (entity=components, type=skill, group_by=["category"]); whether OAuth goes with a better rank (entity=connectors, store=claude, group_by=["auth"], measure=["rank_claude","in_top_100_claude"]). To see what a group has in common, run it with and without the filter for that group and compare.

entity.description: What to count and measure: connectors, tools, inputs (tool parameters) or components (skills, commands, hooks, UI templates...)

group_by.description: Up to 2 fields to break down by. Connector fields work for every entity: store, audience, category, industry, kind, auth, has_ui, has_events (ChatGPT plugin events), mcp_notifications (standard MCP notifications a server declares), keyword (ChatGPT plugin keywords: which keywords a group of connectors uses), has_instructions, skills_over_mcp, host_provider, publisher, has_mcp_server, tools_known, auth_provider, dynamic_registration, cimd, anonymous_tools. Tools add access, access_estimated and source; inputs add type, required, tool_access and tool_source; components add type and component_store

measure.description: Numbers to summarize (min, max, mean, median, p90). connectors: tools (only connectors whose tool list is known), skills, keywords (ChatGPT plugin keywords, only connectors that have some), components, rank_chatgpt, rank_claude, in_top_100_chatgpt, in_top_100_claude (1 or 0, so the mean is the share in the top 100). tools: description_length, inputs. inputs: description_length, enum_values. components: description_length, body_length. Leave out for counts only

q.description: Only rows whose own text matches: a tool, input or component search like in search_tools; for connectors, the connector text

type.description: components: only this component type (skill, command, ui_template...). inputs: only this JSON type (string, number, boolean, array, object)

access.description: tools and inputs: only tools with this access (declared by the server, else estimated from the name)

source.description: tools and inputs: store (the store lists the tool) or server (only the MCP server lists it)

connector.description: Words in the connector's name, company or description, to search one connector or a few

tools.name: list_changes
tools.description: Use this when the user explores changes across many connectors, e.g. which ChatGPT apps added tools this week (store=chatgpt, kinds=["tool_added"], days=7) or which apps were renamed (kinds=["renamed"]). Filter by store, since/until and kinds rather than paging through every change. To show the connectors to the user, call render_connector_table with their slugs (the connector field). For changes to named connectors use get_connector_changelog, which also reports historical coverage.

kinds.description: Change types in one request; omit for all

limit.description: Maximum events per connector per page

cursor.description: next_cursor from the previous page, with the same filters

slug.description: Only this connector; prefer get_connector_changelog for its complete history

kind.description: Legacy single type; use kinds for multiple types. Cannot combine both

days.description: How many days back when since is omitted

intent.description: Always fill in: one sentence on what the user wants and why, in your words. No personal details.

tools.name: list_usage_reports
tools.description: Use this when the user asks about real usage of connectors, plugins or MCP servers, or what usage to expect at a rank. No store publishes usage; this returns the numbers that companies published themselves, with each connector's rank today.

intent.description: Always fill in: one sentence on what the user wants and why, in your words. No personal details.

tools.name: get_guide
tools.description: Use this when the user asks how something works rather than for data: how people discover connectors in ChatGPT and Claude, how to write server instructions, tool descriptions or store listing text, what the store ranks mean, what Agent Ready can and cannot see in each store (data-coverage), or what similar-sounding terms mean (concepts).

topic.description: discovery: how people find connectors in ChatGPT and Claude. server-instructions, tool-descriptions, listing-metadata: how to write each. ranks-explained: what the store ranks mean. data-coverage: what Agent Ready can and cannot see in each store (tools, instructions, sign-in, history). concepts: terms that sound alike (ChatGPT plugin events vs MCP notifications, sign-in vs sign-up, rank vs usage...)

intent.description: Always fill in: one sentence on what the user wants and why, in your words. No personal details.

tools.name: list_stores
tools.description: Use this when the user asks which AI app stores Agent Ready covers, how many connectors each has, or which stores publish a rank.

intent.description: Always fill in: one sentence on what the user wants and why, in your words. No personal details.

tools.name: render_connector_table
tools.description: Use this to show a list of connectors to the user as a table: 5 or more connectors, a ranked or browsed list, the newest connectors, or the connectors in list_changes results (which changed, were added or renamed). Takes slugs from search_connectors, list_changes or get_connector_changelog. Shows logos, descriptions, categories, store ranks and tool counts. To compare 2 to 4 connectors, use render_connector_compare. The user sees the table, so do not repeat its rows as a list or table in your answer: add only what the table does not show, such as what changed.

slugs.description: 1 to 25 slugs from search_connectors, list_changes or get_connector_changelog, in the order to show

intent.description: Always fill in: one sentence on what the user wants and why, in your words. No personal details.

tools.name: render_connector_compare
tools.description: Use this when the user compares or asks about 2 to 4 connectors. Takes slugs from search_connectors, list_changes or the user; known slugs need no search. Shows a card for each, side by side, with stores, rank in ChatGPT and Claude, tool count by type (read, change, destructive), interactive UI and sign-in. For 5 or more, use render_connector_table; for one, render_connector_detail. The user sees every one of these facts on the cards, so do not restate them as a table or list: answer in one to three sentences on what differs and what it means for the user.

slugs.description: 2 to 4 slugs, from search_connectors or another tool, in the order to show

intent.description: Always fill in: one sentence on what the user wants and why, in your words. No personal details.

tools.name: render_connector_detail
tools.description: Use this when the user asks about one connector, plugin, app or MCP server ("tell me about X", "what is X", "show me X"): it shows a card with rank and 30-day trend in each store, capabilities, sign-in, every tool with its inputs, server instructions, screenshots and example prompts. You also get its data, so get_connector is not needed first. Known slugs need no search. The user sees the card, so do not repeat its facts or make your own card: add only what the card does not show.

intent.description: Always fill in: one sentence on what the user wants and why, in your words. No personal details.

tools.name: render_rank_chart
tools.description: Call get_rank_history first. Use this to show one connector's rank over time as a chart, with the same slug, store and dates. The user sees the chart, so do not list the daily ranks in your answer.

store.description: chatgpt or claude: the only stores that publish a rank

from.description: First day (YYYY-MM-DD). Leave out for the whole history

to.description: Last day (YYYY-MM-DD). Leave out for the latest day

intent.description: Always fill in: one sentence on what the user wants and why, in your words. No personal details.

tools.name: send_feedback
tools.description: Use this to send feedback about Agent Ready to its team: wrong or missing data, a tool or widget that broke or confused, a feature request, or praise. Send it when the user asks, or when they agree after you offer it once (source user). You may also report on your own, without asking, when this data looks wrong or missing or a tool result is broken or confusing (source agent): one report per problem, then carry on with the user's task. Do not report your own mistakes, or an error you fixed by changing your call. Leave out personal details, account data and the conversation itself. Nobody replies, so do not promise a reply.

kind.description: What it is about: wrong_data, missing_data, bug (a tool or widget broke), confusing, feature_request, praise or other

message.description: What worked or broke, in the user's words where you can. Name the connector, store or tool it is about. No personal details, account data or conversation text

context.description: What the user was trying to do

tool.description: The Agent Ready tool it is about, if one

connector.description: Slug of the connector it is about, if one

source.description: Who found it. user: the user asked to send this, or agreed when you offered. agent: you are reporting on your own, without asking

intent.description: Always fill in: one sentence on what the user wants and why, in your words. No personal details.
